name: Secure context and cross-origin isolation
plain: Flags telling whether the page is HTTPS and isolated from other origins.
meaning: isSecureContext and crossOriginIsolated are set by the site itself, so they mostly describe the page, not the person. They gate high-power APIs and timer precision (5 microseconds when isolated, 100 microseconds otherwise in Chrome).

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can check whether the page is on HTTPS and isolated, which describes the site, not you
limits.user_action: Nothing. It describes how the site itself was set up
can: Check if the page runs on HTTPS
Check if the page is isolated from other origins
Unlock stronger features and finer timers when both are true
cannot: Tell anything about you or your device
Be changed by you; the site sets it
Unlock powerful features on plain HTTP pages
Give you finer timers unless the site opts in

story.what_it_is: Two yes or no flags showing whether a page is on HTTPS and walled off from other sites.

marketing.name: Making your website cross-origin isolated
marketing.pitch: web.dev explains the isolation switch that unlocks powerful features like shared memory and precise timers.

story.for_you: You never see these flags. They mostly describe how the site is built. If a site turns the isolation on, you may get faster, more powerful pages such as full speed browser games and editors.
story.for_makers: Powerful features like shared memory and fine timers only work on pages that are secure and isolated. Heavy apps flip the switch to run fast. The flags describe the page rather than the person, so they carry little tracking value.

use_cases.example: A browser game engine needs isolation to use shared memory threads, so it runs at a smooth frame rate.
A browser video editor needs it to run fast video code in the page.
A web code editor runs a full programming environment in the tab, which needs the isolation flag.
A browser version of a design app turns on advanced timers and threads for heavy files.
A bank locks down its pages so another site cannot peek into them.
A site monitors how many visitors lack isolation to find broken embeds.

technical_bounds: Describes the page, not the user
